problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\frac{6}{{t}^{3}}$, where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=24\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary. Do not round your answer.

The particle is stationary at $t=$
{{field-1}}$\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{6}{{t}^{3}}\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{3}{{t}^{2}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=24.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}24 & =-\frac{3}{(1)^{2}}+C \\ 24 & =-3+C \\ C & =27.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-\frac{3}{{t}^{2}}+27.$

Now, we find the moments in time when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{{t}^{2}}+27 & =0 \\ \frac{3}{{t}^{2}} & =27 \\ {t}^{2} & =\frac{1}{9} \\ t & =\pm \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t>0$, we discard solution $t=-\frac{1}{3}.$ 

Therefore, the particle is stationary when $t=\frac{1}{3}\,\text{s}.$
